description:
Remote, United States

Full time | Reports to David, CEO

Hey, I'm David, CEO and co-founder of Whippy. I'm hiring a Head of Operations & Chief of Staff to own everything in this company that is not selling, building product, or serving customers, and to build the team and the systems that run it. This is one role, about 70% operations and 30% chief of staff, not two jobs and not a coordinator sitting next to me.

Why I'm hiring

Whippy is bootstrapped, profitable, and the category leader in AI communication for staffing, with over 1,000 customers and new industries opening behind it. We have no board and no outside investors. This is not a role built around investor updates. It is a role built around making the company run.

We got here with a small team and a CEO who still owns too much of the operational layer: quote-to-cash, contracts, payments, revenue operations, recruiting, and the back office. My time needs to go to enterprise customers, new partnerships, new industries, and the hires that change the company. Everything else that routes through me today needs an owner.

The thesis for this role is simple. Learn each piece by doing it yourself. Document it so someone else can run it. Automate it so it runs itself. Hire an Operations Associate to take the first layer from you. Move up to the next piece. A year from now, the operational layer of this company should run without me being asked a question, and you should be the one running it.

What you will own

You run these yourself at first. Then you hire, automate, and keep the system running.

  1. Quote-to-cash automation. Own revenue operations from signed contract to cash collected, and build the automation so it runs itself. Contracts, subscriptions, invoicing, collections, upgrades, and a close that does not need me. The goal is not a better checklist. It is a system that takes a signed deal to cash, accurately, on its own.

  2. Contracts and vendors. Order forms, MSAs, NDAs, renewals, and partner agreements, with a short list of what still comes to me. Vendor renewals, usage, and cost.

  3. Revenue operations. Stand up and maintain our CRM so expansion tracking, partner commissions, and the sales-to-CS handoff actually run through it.

  4. People-ops admin. Commissions, onboarding and offboarding, and recruiting coordination for open roles except final interviews, which stay with me and the hiring manager.

  5. The Operations Associate. In your first 30 to 60 days, you will hire an Operations Associate who takes follow-ups, collections work, and recruiting coordination off both of us. They may be international. Until they start, you do that work yourself. After they start, you manage them.

What this grows into

Once those areas run without reminders, you move toward the work that sits closest to me: my weekly priorities, the operating cadence of the company, and one special project at a time, whether that is pricing, a market, or a partnership. I decide. You drive it to the decision and then make sure it happens.

I will not pretend that is the day one job. It is earned by making the day one job disappear. But the ceiling here is high. If you make the operational layer disappear and take on more of the company, this is a path to COO. I'm hiring for someone who wants that.

What success looks like

  • Days 1 to 60: you own quote-to-cash end to end, including contracts and vendors. The path from signed contract to cash collected is accurate, the first automations are live, and I am no longer in the routine work. You have hired the Operations Associate, or have a finalist in front of me.

  • Days 60 to 120: our CRM is stood up and maintained, partner commissions run through you, and people-ops admin is off my plate. Quote-to-cash largely runs itself, and the associate works off documentation you wrote.

  • After that: the operational layer no longer routes through me, and the chief-of-staff work is a real share of your week: my weekly priorities, the company cadence, and one special project at a time.

  • Year one: the operational layer runs without me, and you have shipped at least one piece of chief-of-staff work that changed a company decision.

How we work

Bootstrapped and profitable, so revenue is the strategy. No task is above or beneath anyone here, including me, and I still cold call. We use AI to move fast, but we own our work and verify every fact. Speed over polish. Results over activity. You will always know where you stand with me.

What I'm looking for

  • You have built an operations function from scratch, not only inherited one, and you have owned quote-to-cash because you have done the work.

  • You can build automation yourself, with workflows or light scripting, and sit with an engineer when the work belongs in the product.

  • You have managed people and built a process that someone else then ran without you.

  • You have worked close to a founder, and sat across from a partner, vendor, or customer, and handled something that mattered.

  • You are very AI-forward. You already use AI tools every day to do your work faster and better, you reach for automation before headcount, and you can show us how.

  • You are willing to be hands-on for the first six months. If you need a team on day one, this is not the role.

  • Organized to a fault, clear in writing, and comfortable being measured on outcomes, not activity.

  • Fluent written and spoken English, and experience at a SaaS company, ideally one that sells to operators rather than to tech companies. Staffing or HR tech is a plus, not a requirement.

Nice to haves

  • Stripe, HubSpot, PandaDoc, Deel, or Rippling.

  • Experience with partner revenue share or usage-based billing.

  • Time in a bootstrapped or founder-led company.

This is not for you if

  • You think the operational work is beneath the title. It is the first six months and how you earn everything after.

  • You want a pure chief of staff job: briefing a founder, running meetings, and handing the work back.

  • You want to coordinate quote-to-cash and then hand the automation to someone else. Building the automation is the job.

  • You prefer to coordinate rather than own. I need someone who closes things, not someone who tracks them.

  • You want a defined scope that does not change, or a team on day one.

About Whippy

Whippy is a communication, automation, and AI agent platform. You reach customers across calls, texts, and email at scale, with every conversation in one shared inbox. Replies get assigned to a teammate, handled by an AI agent, or carried forward by an automation, and the data flows back into your systems in the format you need. It cuts the repetitive work and frees teams for the human work that drives revenue.

We're industry agnostic, with our biggest wins in staffing, healthcare, and other in-person businesses going through digital transformation. We're bootstrapped, profitable, and growing fast, with over 1,000 businesses using Whippy worldwide.

Whippy was founded in 2021 by me and our CTO, Jack Kennedy. Jack is an engineering machine and a marathon runner. I started BloomNation in 2011 after winning $27,205 in a poker tournament, grew it into a platform generating billions in sales for florists, then left to build something bigger with Jack.

Location

Remote, United States. Preference for Los Angeles or New York, where I spend most of my time.

You do not have to work East Coast hours all day. You do need a few hours of overlap with the US East Coast each weekday, roughly 10am to 2pm ET, and you need to be at our all-hands. If you are on the West Coast, that means starting in the morning. Full English fluency required.

Hiring process

  1. You apply and I review it myself.

  2. A 45-minute call with me.

  3. A take-home: I give you a realistic quote-to-cash scenario, and you come back with how you would run it, what you would automate, and how you would hand it off. You present it to me on a 45-minute call.

  4. A 30-minute call with Jack, our CTO.

  5. References, including someone who reported to you.
